findings.issue_text: Verdict: **PASS_ADVISORY** — code-quality, security, test, and architecture reviewers each returned PASS with 0 blocking findings and no advisory/follow-up/warning entries. The only gate signal was in the context pack:
Manifest verdict NEEDS_REVISION — blocker: "missing shard result for shard-01" (all 31 files landed in a single unprocessed shard, so no reviewer actually inspected the diff)
PASS with 0 findings despite the diff adding 5 new modules + 1 new public API route and zero tests — gate did not fire
PASS with 0 findings on a diff that adds an unauthenticated-by-default credential-write API route — gate did not fire

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 — `prisma.credential.update(...)` uses `prisma`, which is never imported in this file (imports end at line 20). TS2304 build failure; at runtime every `new SalesforceCalendarService()` throws ReferenceError inside `getClient()`, so all Salesforce calendar ops break. Confirmed independently. [all 6 lenses]

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97-101 — `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the zod safeParse *wrapper* `{success,data}`, not `.data`; it is written directly to `prisma.credential.update({data:{key}})`. Replaces the old `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` which returned the data. Credential.key becomes `{"success":true,"data":{...}}`; next load, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` at :75 throws and Google Calendar is permanently bricked until re-auth. Fires with the sync flag OFF, i.e. every deployment. [feasibility, intent, completeness, architecture, security]

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29 — webhook auth is `req.headers[name] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. If the secret is unset, both sides are `undefined` and the check passes; `.env.example:237` ships `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET=""`, and an empty header matches `""`. Past the gate the handler writes credentials for an arbitrary body-supplied `userId` — unauthenticated takeover of any user's OAuth credentials. Exploitability hinges on how APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is derived (not in the sliced repo), but the check is unsound regardless. [uncertain on reachability only]

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:32-59 — the team branch checks only `members.some({userId, accepted:true})`, never role, then `return`s; so `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam` at :59 is unreachable for any non-null teamId and always receives `teamId: null`. Any accepted team MEMBER can bind an OAuth credential they control to the whole team via `?state={"teamId":N}` (hubspot/salesforce/stripe/msteams/webex/tandem callbacks).

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15 — the outbound POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT asks for user N's access token with no Authorization header, HMAC, shared secret, or timestamp, even though this same diff introduces CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET for the inbound direction. Anyone who can reach the endpoint can enumerate calcomUserId and harvest tokens.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/{encode,decode}OAuthState.ts:9 — OAuth `state` carries no nonce, no signature, no session binding; `encodeOAuthState` echoes the browser-supplied value verbatim. Account-linking CSRF on the GET callbacks, and it is what makes the teamId escalation above reachable. `returnTo` is separately guarded by getSafeRedirectUrl, so open-redirect is mitigated.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29 — secret compared with `!==` (non-constant-time, short-circuits at first differing byte) with no rate limiting on the route; use crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17,31,57-59 — no `req.method` guard (GET/PUT/DELETE all reach the handler); `.parse` not `.safeParse` throws ZodError on any malformed/absent body; `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` has no try/catch and the `|| ""` key fallback makes createDecipheriv throw "Invalid key length" on every request when the key is unset. All surface as 500s, not 400s. Decrypted `keys` is stored with no schema validation.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:37,46,53 — distinct 404 bodies ("User not found" / "App not found" / "…correct app slug") plus userId echoed in the 200 give a user- and app-enumeration oracle.
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29 — static bearer secret with no timestamp/nonce: a captured request is replayable indefinitely.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-11 — both computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` evaluate to the literal `"[object Object]"` and collide, so minimumTokenResponseSchema is effectively `{access_token: string}`. Because z.object strips unknown keys, sync-mode parsing silently discards expires_in/expiry_date/refresh_token/instance_url/scope. The comment "any property with a number is the expiry" describes behavior that does not exist. Verified empirically by two lenses.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27 — missing refresh_token is defaulted to the literal string `"refresh_token"`, and this sits OUTSIDE the flag check so it runs with sync OFF. office365calendar's schema declares `refresh_token: z.string().optional()` (:56), so o365 :264-272 spreads the sentinel over the real token and persists it; the next refresh POSTs `refresh_token=refresh_token` to Microsoft → invalid_grant, unrecoverable without reinstall.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3-19 — `refreshFunction: () => any` with no declared return type; the sync branch returns a raw fetch Response, the fallback returns each app's SDK shape. The compiler cannot see the mismatch. googlecalendar:94 `res?.data` → undefined → TypeError swallowed by the catch at :103 (silent permanent no-op refresh); hubspot:177-200 annotates the Response as HubspotToken → `expiresIn` undefined → NaN expiryDate → persists a serialized Response as credential.key, inside a `catch { log.error }` that hides it.

refreshOAuthTokens wired into 6 apps but parseRefreshTokenResponse into only 3 — webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:88 still validates against webexRefreshedTokenSchema (requires refresh_token, scope literal, refresh_token_expires_in) so sync always rejects; larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:84-96 expects Lark's `{code,data:{...}}` envelope and persists all-undefined credentials; office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:87-95 *replaces* the whole key with the minimal payload, dropping refresh_token/scope/token_type. Salesforce got the parser but never routes through the sync endpoint at all.

refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5 vs parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15 — the two helpers guard on different conditions (only the former requires truthy userId). For a team credential with sync on, the refresh correctly hits the provider but the response is still validated by the stripping minimum schema. The "is sync active" predicate is expressed three separate ways and should be one function taking the credential.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15 — `response.ok`/status is never checked, so a 401/500/HTML error page from the sync endpoint is handed downstream as if it were a token payload.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-99 — a brand-new unconditional token refresh + prisma write inserted into getClient(), which the constructor calls (:57). No expiry check, no flag gate, and it bypasses refreshOAuthTokens entirely — so the one app given a new refresh is the one app excluded from the feature this PR is named after. Adds a blocking login.salesforce.com round-trip and a credential write to every booking/availability call.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:101-108 — the refreshed token is then discarded: the jsforce.Connection is still built from the stale `credentialKey.access_token`/`instance_url` read before the refresh. The network call and DB write accomplish nothing for the caller.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:86 — `response.statusText !== "OK"` is not a success check; statusText is empty under undici/HTTP-2, so a successful 200 throws HttpError with an empty message. Use `response.ok`. Rejection inside a constructor-stored promise also risks an unhandled rejection.

packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17 — `appConfig.slug` replaced with a hardcoded `"zoho-bigin"` literal while :12 and :22 still read appConfig; unrelated to the stated scope and reintroduces slug/redirect-URI drift. (appConfig stays used, so no unused-import break.)

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263 — parse failure now THROWS where it previously console.error'd the zodError plus the raw MS response and continued with stale credentials. refreshAccessToken and getToken have no try/catch, so a malformed-but-200 Microsoft response becomes a hard failure in the booking path, with neither the zod issues nor the payload in the message.

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264 and packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:92-94 — dead `.success` branches: the helper throws on failure, so `success` is always true. Left in at salesforce, half-cleaned at o365 — same transformation, opposite treatment in one PR.
.env.example:259 — trailing-newline-only hunk, incidental churn. (trivial)

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:61-92 — check-then-act with no unique constraint and no transaction; the code's own comment concedes "Can't use prisma upsert as we don't know the id", and larkcalendar/api/callback.ts:54-60 independently documents that (userId, type) is not unique. Two concurrent deliveries both create, leaving duplicate credentials. Needs a unique index on (userId, appId) + upsert, or $transaction with row locking.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62-66 — `findFirst` has no orderBy and no invalid/teamId filter; a user with two accounts of the same app (two Google Calendars) can have the wrong row overwritten non-deterministically.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:73-80 — `data: { key: keys }` replaces the JSON blob wholesale. If the caller sends only `{access_token, expiry_date}` (the shape refreshOAuthTokens:7 documents), refresh_token/instance_url/email/scope are lost. Contrast salesforce:98, which merges precisely because it knows the payload is lossy.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:64-72 — the update never resets `invalid`, yet googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:112-117 in this same diff sets `invalid: true` on invalid_grant. The intended recovery flow (parent app pushes fresh keys) does not re-enable the credential.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts — no teamId support at all, though createOAuthAppCredential.ts:47-54 in this same PR creates team credentials; team-owned credentials can never be synced and .env.example does not state the limitation.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:34 — `prisma.user.findUnique({where:{id}})` with no `select` pulls every user column (password hash, 2FA secret, identity-provider tokens) just to test existence; should be `select: {id: true}`.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:40-50 — the app lookup selects only `slug`, which equals the `where` clause by construction, so `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]` is identical to `appStoreMetadata[reqBody.appSlug]`; the round-trip's only value is an existence check that never verifies `app.enabled`.

refreshOAuthTokens call sites — app slugs are hardcoded string literals ("google-calendar", "hubspot", "lark-calendar", "office365-calendar", "msteams", "webex") rather than read from each config.json, with no compile-time link to the appSlug the webhook validates. webex/api/callback.ts:17 already demonstrates the `config.slug` pattern. ("msteams" is the genuine slug — it just isn't type-checked.)

credential `key` read-modify-write has no optimistic concurrency (webex:93-107, o365calendar:264-272, o365video:87-95, lark:98-105, google:98-101). Two concurrent bookings both refresh, last-write-wins; for rotating-refresh-token providers (Webex, Lark, Microsoft) the losing writer held the valid token and the credential dies.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/encodeOAuthState.ts:5-12 — JSON.parse immediately followed by JSON.stringify on the same value returns the input verbatim; it is decodeOAuthState plus a stringify, so the pair is one function duplicated, and the name promises encoding that never happens. If a signed/opaque state was the intent, it is unimplemented.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:42 — `members: {select:{userId:true}}` is fetched and never used (materializes every membership row); :13 JSDoc says "@param appData.type the app slug" when type is the app *type* ("hubspot_other_calendar") and appId is the slug.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:6 — imports `"../oauth/decodeOAuthState"` from inside `_utils/oauth/`; resolves, but should be `"./decodeOAuthState"` — evidence the path rewrite was mechanical.
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:16 — leftover empty `/** */` stub comment.

No tests anywhere for the new surface — no test file for the webhook handler, refreshOAuthTokens, or parseRefreshTokenResponse. The zod-key collapse, the safeParse-wrapper persistence, the Response/SDK type mismatch, and the dead admin guard are all first-assertion-level failures a single unit test on each helper would have caught. (Repo is a 31-file slice, so I can't evidence the repo's test convention — but the diff itself adds none.)

Migration completeness — the diff adds _utils/oauth/{encodeOAuthState,decodeOAuthState,createOAuthAppCredential}.ts with no deletion or rename of the originals at _utils/. Within the slice no stale imports remain, but cal.com has further OAuth apps (zoho-crm, zohocalendar, pipedrive, closecom, vital) that import the old paths. Either two divergent copies now exist — so a future fix to the team-authorization bug lands in only half the app store — or the originals were removed out-of-band and every unmigrated caller fails to build. [uncertain — needs the unsliced tree]

.env.example:236-244 — self-contradictory guidance: the comment says the encryption key "must be 32 bytes for AES256" while suggesting `openssl rand -base64 24`, seven lines below a `openssl rand -base64 32` suggestion for the webhook secret. `-base64 24` does yield a working 32-char key (but only 192 bits of entropy); an operator who copies the nearby 32 command gets 44 chars → "Invalid key length" → unhandled 500 on every webhook call. No startup or runtime validation of key length.

Two notes on what the lenses deliberately cleared rather than reported: prototype pollution via `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]` is not exploitable (the slug is read back from an `App` row, so an attacker cannot introduce `__proto__`), and duplicate headers fold into a comma-joined string in Node rather than an array, so that path fails closed. Pre-existing open redirects at `stripepayment/api/callback.ts:51` and `larkcalendar/api/callback.ts:98` are reachable via the unvalidated state but are not introduced by this diff.

Bottom line: two hard blockers (the missing `prisma` import and the Google credential corruption) mean this does not build and would brick Google Calendar credentials on the default path, and the credential-sync feature itself does not work correctly for any of the six apps it wires up. The deterministic gates reported PASS because shard-01 was never processed.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Verdict: **PASS_ADVISORY** — code-quality, security, test, and architecture reviewers each returned PASS with 0 blocking findings and no advisory/follow-up/warning entries. The only gate signal was in the context pack:

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding does not identify any specific defect in the diff; it explicitly states all reviewers returned PASS with 0 blocking findings and no advisories. Since it contains no claim of a bug/security/correctness issue to verify against the code changes, it cannot be a real, verifiable problem present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Manifest verdict NEEDS_REVISION — blocker: "missing shard result for shard-01" (all 31 files landed in a single unprocessed shard, so no reviewer actually inspected the diff)

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding is about the review/CI process (“missing shard result for shard-01”, “diff landed in a single unprocessed shard”), not a defect introduced by the code changes. Nothing in the unified diff shows shard configuration, manifest/shard outputs, or any missing review artifact; therefore it cannot be verified as a real problem present in the code diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PASS with 0 findings despite the diff adding 5 new modules + 1 new public API route and zero tests — gate did not fire

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add multiple new modules and a new public API route, and it does not add any tests. However, the proposed finding asserts that a review/CI “gate did not fire” and that this should have prevented a PASS, which is not something verifiable from the code diff itself. Lack of accompanying tests is also not, by itself, a clear defect unless the repository has an explicit requirement shown in the diff (it does not). Therefore this finding is about process expectations rather than a concrete, diff-provable bug/security/correctness issue introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PASS with 0 findings on a diff that adds an unauthenticated-by-default credential-write API route — gate did not fire

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new credential-write API route (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`) that authorizes solely by comparing a request header to `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. There is no check that `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is actually set to a non-empty value. Given `.env.example` introduces `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET=""` as the default/example, if credential sharing is enabled (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` true) and the secret remains empty, an attacker can satisfy the check by sending the header with an empty value ("" == ""), allowing credential creation/update. This is a verifiable auth bypass/misconfiguration risk introduced by the diff; however whether the feature flag is enabled by default is not shown in the diff, so the "by-default gate did not fire" phrasing is only partially supported.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 — `prisma.credential.update(...)` uses `prisma`, which is never imported in this file (imports end at line 20). TS2304 build failure; at runtime every `new SalesforceCalendarService()` throws ReferenceError inside `getClient()`, so all Salesforce calendar ops break. Confirmed independently. [all 6 lenses]

adjudication.rationale: The diff snippet for `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts` only shows changes near the top of the file (imports and a new `salesforceTokenSchema`) and then truncates before any methods/logic where `prisma.credential.update(...)` would appear. While `prisma` is indeed not imported in the shown import list, the finding’s core claim (that `prisma.credential.update(...)` is used at ~line 96 and thus causes TS2304/ReferenceError) is not verifiable from the provided diff content because that referenced code is not present in the diff excerpt.

Fires with the sync flag OFF, i.e. every deployment. [feasibility, intent, completeness, architecture, security]
matched_golden_ids: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

This matches the golden comment’s issue about storing the wrapper rather than the token data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15 — the outbound POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT asks for user N's access token with no Authorization header, HMAC, shared secret, or timestamp, even though this same diff introduces CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET for the inbound direction. Anyone who can reach the endpoint can enumerate calcomUserId and harvest tokens.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `refreshOAuthTokens` which, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, POSTs to that endpoint with only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body and no authentication material (no Authorization header, signature/HMAC, timestamp/nonce, etc.). While the actual exploitability depends on how the self-hoster secures their endpoint, the lack of any auth in the shipped code path is directly verifiable in the diff and is a reasonable security finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/{encode,decode}OAuthState.ts:9 — OAuth `state` carries no nonce, no signature, no session binding; `encodeOAuthState` echoes the browser-supplied value verbatim. adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29 — secret compared with `!==` (non-constant-time, short-circuits at first differing byte) with no rate limiting on the route; use crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers.

adjudication.rationale: The new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` authenticates solely by comparing a shared secret from an HTTP header to `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` using `!==` (lines shown in the diff). This is a normal JS string/primitive comparison (not constant-time) and therefore is susceptible to timing side-channels in principle when used for secrets. The suggestion to use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` for equal-length buffers is applicable. The part about “no rate limiting on the route” is not shown in this diff (there could be global/middleware rate limiting), but the non-constant-time secret comparison itself is directly verifiable in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17,31,57-59 — no `req.method` guard (GET/PUT/DELETE all reach the handler); `.parse` not `.safeParse` throws ZodError on any malformed/absent body; `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` has no try/catch and the `|| ""` key fallback makes createDecipheriv throw "Invalid key length" on every request when the key is unset. All surface as 500s, not 400s. Decrypted `keys` is stored with no schema validation.
matched_golden_ids: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly notes that using `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` (not `safeParse`) will throw a ZodError on malformed/absent bodies, which would surface as a 500 instead of a 400. This is the same core issue described in the golden comment, though the candidate also adds additional related 500-causing problems.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:37,46,53 — distinct 404 bodies ("User not found" / "App not found" / "…correct app slug") plus userId echoed in the 200 give a user- and app-enumeration oracle.

adjudication.rationale: The handler returns different 404 messages for missing user/app/metadata and echoes userId in 200 responses, but those responses are only reachable after passing a shared-secret header check (`req.headers[CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME] === CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) and after `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is true. Without the secret, every request is stopped with a generic 403 (“Invalid webhook secret”), so the endpoint does not provide an enumeration oracle to unauthenticated callers. The proposed finding omits this gating and overstates the impact.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29 — static bearer secret with no timestamp/nonce: a captured request is replayable indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler authenticates solely by comparing a single static shared secret in a request header (`req.headers[...]==process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). There is no per-request signature, timestamp, nonce, or idempotency/replay protection. Therefore, any previously valid request (body + header) can be replayed later and will again be accepted and will update/create credentials, making replay feasible if a request is captured or the secret is leaked.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-11 — both computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` evaluate to the literal `"[object Object]"` and collide, so minimumTokenResponseSchema is effectively `{access_token: string}`. Because z.object strips unknown keys, sync-mode parsing silently discards expires_in/expiry_date/refresh_token/instance_url/scope. The comment "any property with a number is the expiry" describes behavior that does not exist. Verified empirically by two lenses.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27 — missing refresh_token is defaulted to the literal string `"refresh_token"`, and this sits OUTSIDE the flag check so it runs with sync OFF. office365calendar's schema declares `refresh_token: z.string().optional()` (:56), so o365 :264-272 spreads the sentinel over the real token and persists it; the next refresh POSTs `refresh_token=refresh_token` to Microsoft → invalid_grant, unrecoverable without reinstall.
matched_golden_ids: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue describes the same bug: when the OAuth refresh token response lacks a refresh_token, parseRefreshTokenResponse defaults it to the literal string "refresh_token", which then gets persisted and used in subsequent refresh requests, causing invalid_grant/auth failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3-19 — `refreshFunction: () => any` with no declared return type; the sync branch returns a raw fetch Response, the fallback returns each app's SDK shape. The compiler cannot see the mismatch. googlecalendar:94 `res?.data` → undefined → TypeError swallowed by the catch at :103 (silent permanent no-op refresh); hubspot:177-200 annotates the Response as HubspotToken → `expiresIn` undefined → NaN expiryDate → persists a serialized Response as credential.key, inside a `catch { log.error }` that hides it.
matched_golden_ids: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core bug: in the sync-enabled branch `refreshFunction` returns a raw `fetch` Response, while callers (e.g., Google expecting `res.data`, Hubspot expecting a `HubspotToken`) assume an integration-specific token object. It also notes the resulting runtime failures/silent errors, aligning with the golden comment’s mismatch concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5 vs parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15 — the two helpers guard on different conditions (only the former requires truthy userId). For a team credential with sync on, the refresh correctly hits the provider but the response is still validated by the stripping minimum schema. The "is sync active" predicate is expressed three separate ways and should be one function taking the credential.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15 — `response.ok`/status is never checked, so a 401/500/HTML error page from the sync endpoint is handed downstream as if it were a token payload.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, it performs a `fetch(...)` and immediately `return response;` without checking `response.ok` or status. This makes it possible for a 401/500 or non-JSON/HTML error response from the sync endpoint to flow downstream without being rejected at the boundary of `refreshOAuthTokens`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:61-92 — check-then-act with no unique constraint and no transaction; the code's own comment concedes "Can't use prisma upsert as we don't know the id", and larkcalendar/api/callback.ts:54-60 independently documents that (userId, type) is not unique. Two concurrent deliveries both create, leaving duplicate credentials. Needs a unique index on (userId, appId) + upsert, or $transaction with row locking.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts the handler does a non-atomic "findFirst -> if exists update else create" on credential records keyed by { userId, appId }. With concurrent webhook deliveries for the same (userId, appSlug), both requests can observe no existing record and both run prisma.credential.create(), producing duplicates if the database does not enforce uniqueness. The code comment "Can't use prisma upsert as we don't know the id" strongly implies there is no usable unique constraint for an upsert on these fields, which makes the duplication scenario a concrete correctness issue introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62-66 — `findFirst` has no orderBy and no invalid/teamId filter; a user with two accounts of the same app (two Google Calendars) can have the wrong row overwritten non-deterministically.

adjudication.rationale: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts the code looks up an existing credential via `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId: reqBody.userId, appId: appMetadata.slug } })` and then updates that single row. Because `findFirst` is used (not `findUnique`) and there is no `orderBy`, if more than one credential row exists for the same `(userId, appId)` pair, which the code itself implicitly allows by not using an upsert/unique key, the selected row is not guaranteed to be deterministic and the webhook could overwrite an unintended credential. The finding’s mention of a missing teamId filter is not supported by the diff (userId filter already excludes typical team credentials), but the non-deterministic overwrite risk from `findFirst` is real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:73-80 — `data: { key: keys }` replaces the JSON blob wholesale. If the caller sends only `{access_token, expiry_date}` (the shape refreshOAuthTokens:7 documents), refresh_token/instance_url/email/scope are lost. Contrast salesforce:98, which merges precisely because it knows the payload is lossy.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:64-72 — the update never resets `invalid`, yet googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:112-117 in this same diff sets `invalid: true` on invalid_grant. The intended recovery flow (parent app pushes fresh keys) does not re-enable the credential.

adjudication.rationale: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts, when an existing credential is found, the update call only sets `data: { key: keys }` and does not clear any `invalid` flag. If a credential had previously been marked invalid (the finding cites googlecalendar code in this diff setting `invalid: true` on `invalid_grant`), then pushing fresh keys via this webhook would leave the credential still marked invalid, preventing recovery via “parent app pushes fresh keys.” This is directly verifiable from the webhook handler’s update/create payloads in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts — no teamId support at all, though createOAuthAppCredential.ts:47-54 in this same PR creates team credentials; team-owned credentials can never be synced and .env.example does not state the limitation.

adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` only accepts `userId` (schema: `{ userId, appSlug, keys }`), validates a `prisma.user` by that ID, and then reads/updates/creates `prisma.credential` records only via `where: { userId: reqBody.userId, appId: appMetadata.slug }`. There is no request field or lookup path for `teamId`, and no query/update on a team-owned credential. In the same diff, `createOAuthAppCredential` is described/used as creating credentials for either a user or a team, so team-owned credentials exist in this system but cannot be synced via this webhook as implemented. The `.env.example` comments added for credential sync do not mention that only user-owned credentials are supported.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:34 — `prisma.user.findUnique({where:{id}})` with no `select` pulls every user column (password hash, 2FA secret, identity-provider tokens) just to test existence; should be `select: {id: true}`.

adjudication.rationale: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts the handler does `const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: reqBody.userId } });` and then only checks `if (!user)`. With Prisma, omitting `select` returns the full user row by default, meaning the query fetches all user columns even though only existence (or id) is needed. This is a verifiable inefficiency and can unnecessarily load sensitive fields into memory for this request path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:40-50 — the app lookup selects only `slug`, which equals the `where` clause by construction, so `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]` is identical to `appStoreMetadata[reqBody.appSlug]`; the round-trip's only value is an existence check that never verifies `app.enabled`.

While `app.slug` will equal `reqBody.appSlug` if the row exists (so returning `slug` is redundant), the query is still serving a concrete purpose: verifying the app exists in the database. The proposed issue about never verifying `app.enabled` is not verifiable from the diff (no `enabled` field is shown/used), so it’s speculative rather than a clear defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: credential `key` read-modify-write has no optimistic concurrency (webex:93-107, o365calendar:264-272, o365video:87-95, lark:98-105, google:98-101). Two concurrent bookings both refresh, last-write-wins; for rotating-refresh-token providers (Webex, Lark, Microsoft) the losing writer held the valid token and the credential dies.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows multiple integrations refreshing OAuth tokens and then persisting the updated credential with `prisma.credential.update({ where: { id }, data: { key } })` based on an in-memory copy of the prior credential (e.g., GoogleCalendarService refresh writes `key` after mutating `googleCredentials`; Office365CalendarService merges refreshed fields into `o365AuthCredentials` then updates; Lark/Hubspot/O365 video follow similar patterns). There is no version/updatedAt check or transactional guard tying the update to the credential state that was refreshed, so concurrent refreshes can race and cause last-write-wins. For providers that rotate refresh tokens, the “losing” writer may overwrite a newly-rotated refresh token with an older one, breaking future refreshes. While the finding cites Webex which is not in this diff, the core race condition it describes is verifiably present in the shown refresh-and-update flows.

If a signed/opaque state was the intent, it is unimplemented.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:42 — `members: {select:{userId:true}}` is fetched and never used (materializes every membership row); :13 JSDoc says "@param appData.type the app slug" when type is the app *type* ("hubspot_other_calendar") and appId is the slug.
